title: Blood transfusion
what: Blood from a donor, or a part of it, is given into your vein through a drip: red cells, plasma, or platelets.
why: For severe anemia, major blood loss, during surgery, or with some blood disorders.
duration: one unit usually takes 1 to 4 hours, plus observation
tell_doctor: If you had transfusions before and any reactions to them
If you are against transfusion for personal or religious reasons, say so in advance

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before a transfusion, your blood type is checked and a compatibility test is done. This is required.

prepare.title: Consent
prepare.text: Your doctor explains why you need the transfusion, and you sign a consent form.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually eat and drink as usual, unless your doctor says otherwise.

bring: Past discharge papers that show your blood type and transfusions
steps: Blood is taken to check your type and compatibility
An IV line is put in a vein
At your bedside, the nurse and doctor check your name against the label on the bag
Your blood type is checked again before starting
For the first minutes, the blood drips slowly, and you are watched closely
Your blood pressure, pulse, and temperature are checked regularly
feel: Sometimes chills or a fever. Tell the nurse right away
after: You are usually watched for a while longer
A blood test is done after some time
Sometimes a reaction happens in the first 24 hours after. Tell your doctor if you feel unwell in any way
red_flags: During the transfusion: chills, fever, back or chest pain, shortness of breath, or a rash. Call the nurse right away
At home in the first 24 hours: shortness of breath, dark urine, yellow skin, or a high fever. Call emergency services

faq.q: Can I catch an infection from a transfusion?
faq.a: Donor blood is tested for infections. The risk is very low. Your doctor can tell you more.

faq.q: Can I donate blood for a relative?
faq.a: Sometimes yes, but the blood center decides. A relative's blood goes through all the same checks.

reminders.text: Blood transfusion today. Bring your documents. If you had transfusions before, tell your doctor.
